subject: Emergency: short-notice keystore I/O bridge patch and customer verification
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@acmepay.com>
Cc: ops@acmepay.com
Date: Sat, 11 Feb 2028 08:17:00 -0800
Subject: Emergency: short-notice keystore I/O bridge patch and customer verification

Samir —

I wanted to reach out directly: we just identified a keystore I/O regression in the 0.9.x bridge that can intermittently fail on long-running streaming sessions for Dedicated customers. The engineering team validated a small binary patch that closes the window where the loader could hit a partial write and block on retry. We are planning a short maintenance window in ~45 minutes to push the fix for affected pools and run a targeted smoke test.

What this means for Acme Payments: you may see transient tokenization errors (HTTP 502 / "keystore timeout") on a small subset of requests during the deployment. There is no data corruption risk — this is an availability issue only.

What we need from you, if possible:
- Please run your quick smoke test (payloads used in production) 30 minutes after we confirm completion.
- If you see continued tokenization failures, reply with the sample request IDs (X-Req-Id header) so we can do immediate tracebacks.

We attached the patch (redwood_keystore-io-bridge-0.9.3.patch) and a short action-items doc that lists the verification steps we will ask customers to run. I will send a follow-up when the patch is done and include rollback instructions if necessary.

Apologies for the short notice — the fix reduces error surface quickly, and the risk window grows with time. We prioritized a minimal blast radius and will only target the Dedicated pools serving Acme's region.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Sr. Technical Account Manager, Redwood Inference
marcus@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: redwood_keystore-io-bridge-0.9.3.patch (binary patch stub), customer-action-items-20280211.md (text)

Samir

Date: Sat, 11 Feb 2028 08:35:00 -0800
Subject: URGENT: deploy plan and rollback for keystore I/O bridge patch (0.9.3)

Team —

Quick plan below (we've got ~45 minutes):
- Target pool: us-west-2-dedicated-pool-17 (only Acme's instances)
- Change: apply redwood_keystore-io-bridge-0.9.3.patch to runtime image, restart inflight workers with a draining window of 60s
- Verification (post-deploy): run 200 sample tokenization requests against /v1/tokenize (script attached in customer-action-items-20280211.md)
- Rollback: if error rate > 0.5% on verification or >5 incidents of HTTP 502 in first 10m, execute canary rollback (image previous tag) and re-open pool to traffic
- Communication: Marcus to notify customer and ops; Marissa to coordinate SRE console checks and telemetry; Rishi to lead rollback if we hit the threshold

I've included a one-liner for the CS message and a script snippet in the attachment. Keep replies short — if you have authority to hit rollback, do it and immediately mark the incident with SUP-8693.

-Marcus

Attachments: customer-action-items-20280211.md (verification script and comms blurb)

Subject: Follow-up: keystore I/O bridge patch complete + short postmortem and next steps

Samir —

Following up to confirm the patch deployment completed successfully. Summary:
- Window: Sat 11 Feb 2028 08:50 — 08:55 PST.
- Scope: us-west-2-dedicated-pool-17 (Acme Payments traffic).
- Impact observed: ~3 transient 502s during worker restarts; all resolved within 90s. No persistent failures.
- Actions taken: deployed redwood_keystore-io-bridge-0.9.3, ran verification script, monitored traces.

What we recommend you do now (optional but helpful):
1) Run your smoke test from the action-items doc (we included a curl script and expected response patterns).
2) If you observe any tokenization failures, send the X-Req-Id values to this thread (examples we saw: req-20280211-43a).

We've also prepared a short postmortem draft that covers root cause and the permanent fix schedule (targeting 0.10.0 in the next minor release). You can find it here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1KeystoreHotfixDocs

Thank you again for the quick coordination and for standing by during the window. If you'd like a short sync to walk through the traces with our SREs, we can schedule 30m tomorrow morning.

Best,
Marcus Lin
Sr. Technical Account Manager, Redwood Inference
marcus@redwood.com
